newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 24.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 24.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Mounting concerns about the loss of both two top executives and an equity stake in terrestrial digital TV sent shares in pay-television giant BSkyB diving further on Monday and analysts forecasts more weakness to come. Around 1.7 billion pounds ($2.8 billion) has been wiped off the value of British Sky Broadcasting since last week and some analysts said the shares, which fell 14.5p to 483p in afternoon trade, could tumble to 350p. News Corp Ltd is the largest shareholder in BSkyB. News' U.S. ADRs rose 1/8 to 18 7/8 against a slumping market.

Oil and gas explorer Petroz NL said on Monday drilling encountered a gross gas column of about 85 metres in the Hingkip-1 well in the Timor Sea Zone of Cooperation (ZOCA)."Preliminary analysis suggest a higher liquid content in the gas at Hingkip compared to the Bayu-Undan Field," Petroz said. The well's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, has a 42.417 percent stake while Santos Ltd has 21.426 percent and Indonesia's Inpex Sahul 21.209 percent.

Hawker shares closed 6 cents above Austrim's takeover bid price of A$1.60 per share on Monday. Hawker Richardson said the bid was a "bit low" and the company later advised shareholders to take no action until further notice. Austrim said the bid was fully priced and that the company was not considering increasing it.

Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc on Monday put about 52 percent of its Australian subsidiary on the auction block in a global offering it hopes will raise over A$2 billion. But even as ICI Plc and ICI Australia executives prepare to drum up interest from institutional investors in the offer, the British group said it would consider a bid for its entire stake. * Broken Hill Pty Co ltd A$19.50 (-0.35)
Copper prices ended more than $50 weaker but well off the day's lows on Monday after a rollercoaster session which also saw zinc shoot up to fresh 6-3/4 year highs.
Kilkenny Gold NL said late on Monday it would make a conditional takeover bid for Kalmet Resources Nl. Kilkenny said the offer valued Kalmet at about 29 cents a share or A$23 million.

News' Fox/Liberty Networks has agreed to invest $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow Media Holdings Inc's sports interests, the companies said Monday. The companies will form an equally owned national sports television programming venture that will reach 55 million homes under the name FOX Sports Net. Also, Fox/Liberty will contribute $850 million for a 40 percent equity interest in a new joint venture that will own Rainbow's regional sports networks, which operate under the name SportsChannel, and the Madison Square Garden business.
